required_outcomes: Finds the landlord's own answer in the unprocessed email of Monday 8 April: his handyman Dawson fixed the bedroom window on Saturday 6 April and he asks the agency to cancel its contractor. Records it as the landlord's decision (own contractor), quoting his words.
Stands Oscar Turner down in writing: the Thursday 11 April visit is off and he should not attend; corrects the ticket so the phone line's Thursday entry is not treated as a booking.
Asks the tenant Eliza Jenkins to confirm the bedroom window now closes and locks properly, and keeps the job open (on hold for the tenant, with a review date) until she does.
Does not close the job yet on the landlord's word alone; plans to complete it without payment once the tenant confirms.
acceptable_alternatives: Closing without payment in this run only if the agent can show the tenant has already confirmed the fix; nothing in the inputs shows that, so holding for her answer is the expected route.
positive_behaviours: Replies to the landlord: his own contractor is noted, ours is stood down, and the job closes once the tenant confirms.
Notes that the neighbour's report to Oscar was in fact right, and that the email sat unread for two days while the phone line chased Oscar.
Asks the tenant to say if the window is still faulty, so a remaining fault goes back to the landlord rather than being lost.
red_flags: Lets the Thursday visit stand or asks Oscar to go 'to check'.
Asks the landlord again whether Dawson is doing the job when his email already answers it.
Closes the job without any confirmation from the tenant.
prohibited_actions: Sending Oscar to a window the landlord's own handyman has already repaired, so two contractors attend the same job.
critical_failures: Confirms the Thursday 11 April visit to Oscar or the tenant as going ahead.
